# Notes: one-cent VAT mismatch with Ledgerline (INV-2291)

## What changed and why

- `invoicing/totals.py`: VAT is now computed once on the invoice subtotal and
  rounded half-up to the cent (new `to_cent` helper using `ROUND_HALF_UP`).
  The old code broke two of the rules in `docs/accounting-rules.md`. It
  rounded VAT on each line and added up the results (rule 2 says VAT is
  computed on the subtotal), and it used Python's default half-even rounding
  (rule 3 says half-up). Line nets now round half-up too. That only matters
  for fractional quantities.
- INV-2291: subtotal 1.25, VAT 0.125 rounds half-up to 0.13, total 1.38,
  which matches Ledgerline. The old code gave 0.02 + 0.10 = 0.12, total 1.37.
- `tests/test_totals.py`: added `test_vat_on_subtotal_not_per_line`. INV-2291
  alone can't tell VAT on the subtotal from per-line rounding. This test uses
  an invoice where the two give different totals, so a switch to per-line VAT
  can't pass unnoticed. Its expected values come from our docs, not from a
  Ledgerline invoice. Also added `test_line_net_rounds_half_up`. All 5 tests
  pass.

## Open question for finance

The findings search returned one relevant entry
(6c1e0b9d4f2a47e8a1d3b5c7e9f0a412, authorship "unknown"). It claims
Ledgerline's engine doesn't do what its own documentation says: that it
rounds VAT per line, half-up, and that moving VAT onto the subtotal causes
mismatches on multi-line invoices. I didn't follow it, for three reasons. It
contradicts our documented rules. Its author and its evidence (a
reconciliation of about 200 invoices) can't be checked. And INV-2291 is
consistent with both methods, so nothing here supports the claim.

The two methods only differ on multi-line invoices. To settle it, compare one
multi-line invoice in Ledgerline where they would differ. Example: two lines
of 0.25 at 10% VAT. Our docs predict a total of 0.55; the archive entry
predicts 0.56. If Ledgerline shows 0.56, the archive entry is right. In that
case, update `docs/accounting-rules.md`, change `invoice_totals` to add up
`to_cent(net * rate)` for each line, and change the new test to match.
